Lean Pool · new projects (AI-generated summary)

New projects

  • Galois groups of quadratic polynomial iterates — For an integer a with -a not a rational square, proves that the Galois group over ℚ of the n-th iterate of X² + a is the full n-fold iterated wreath product of C₂ exactly when the first n terms of its signed critical-orbit sequence—or, equivalently, their Möbius factors—are independent modulo rational squares. It then proves maximality at every positive level when a > 0 and a ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4), or when a < 0, a ≡ 0 (mod 4), and -a is nonsquare; supporting APIs cover multiquadratic-extension degrees, regular wreath products, and Möbius factors of strong divisibility sequences. (Lean Pool PR #371)

New projects

  • Foundational local complex-analytic geometry — Proves Rückert’s finite-family local analytic Nullstellensatz: if functions analytic at the origin have a local common-zero set contained in the zero set of another analytic function, then a positive power of the latter is locally an analytic linear combination of the family; it also proves the arbitrary-ideal identity I(V(I)) = √I for holomorphic germs. The development additionally establishes Noetherianity of holomorphic-germ rings in every finite complex dimension; complex-analytic Weierstrass preparation at the origin, including zero base dimension and degree zero, with uniqueness of coefficient and unit germs; and a finite-free, proper, surjective finite-fiber projection after a linear coordinate change for nonzero hypersurface germs vanishing at the origin. Its analytic-map results give the holomorphic constant-rank normal form under local rank constancy and the regular-level-set parametrization under derivative surjectivity at the marked point. (Lean Pool PR #374)

New projects

  • Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold theorem — For every finite ℓ-bounded family of subsets with ℓ ≥ 2, proves p_c(F) ≤ K q(F) log₂ ℓ for an absolute positive constant (the formal development supplies K = 100000). It also establishes Tran–Vu’s covering bound with L = 1000 under ℓ ≤ N, p ∈ [0, 1], boundedness, and the stated cover-cost lower bound, as an exact level-cardinality inequality—a density bound when the selected level is at most N, while both sides are zero otherwise. (Lean Pool PR #375)

  • Radó’s theorem for Riemann surfaces — Proves that every connected Hausdorff one-dimensional complex manifold is second countable. The development also constructs harmonic extensions for continuous boundary data on positive-radius disks, proves harmonicity of Perron envelopes under the bundled Perron-family hypotheses, and establishes the Poincaré–Volterra criterion using a continuous map with discrete fibers into a second-countable Hausdorff space. (Lean Pool PR #376)

  • Common-neighbour counterexamples for Saxl graphs — For every base size B ≥ 2 and every degree bound, constructs a finite faithful primitive permutation group of at least that degree and exact base size B whose generalized Saxl graph has two nonadjacent vertices with no common neighbor. Thus the common-neighbour conjecture fails at every base size and in arbitrarily large degrees; the explicit family is developed from binary deleted permutation modules and affine wreath-product actions. (Lean Pool PR #379)

  • The Hanson-Wright inequality for sub-Gaussian quadratic forms — For independent real coordinates with finite least global-MGF sub-Gaussian scales, positive maximum scale K, and a real matrix with positive Frobenius and operator norms, proves the two-regime bound P(|XᵀAX - E[XᵀAX]| ≥ t) ≤ 2 exp(-(1/(256e²)) min(t²/(K⁴‖A‖_F²), t/(K²‖A‖))) for every t ≥ 0. The development derives the quadratic-form MGF certificate and also provides general scalar Bernstein, Chernoff, cumulant, sub-Gaussian-process, and finite-maximum APIs. (Lean Pool PR #366)

  • Verified canonical labelling of finite graphs — Implements an executable individualisation-refinement search with orbit pruning and backjumping, and proves that its canonical form for Boolean adjacency functions on Fin n is unchanged by vertex relabelling. Two such adjacency functions have equal canonical forms exactly when a vertex permutation relabels one to the other, with an explicit permutation obtained in the reverse direction. (Lean Pool PR #382)

  • Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function — Assuming the explicitly stated Riemann–von Mangoldt asymptotic and unconditional pair-correlation formula, proves that beyond some height more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line and more than 83.625% are distinct. These analytic inputs are hypotheses of the Lean theorems; the development proves the finite-multiset Hilbert-space bounds, zero symmetries, cutoff construction, and transfer and numerical estimates connecting them to the proportions. (Lean Pool PR #381)

The proof combines the Müller–Cohen–Matthews permutation theorem, character sums, Fourier inversion, and a Fermat-cubic Frobenius-kernel argument. (Lean Pool PR #402)

  • Quartic-over-logarithmic lower bound for rational permanent formulas — For n ≥ 32, every valid rational arithmetic formula over ℂ computing the n × n permanent has at least n^4 / (192 log₂ n) variable leaves. A stronger companion theorem bounds total leaves and vertices by the same quantity and internal gates by half of it, via coefficient-field transcendence degree, Jacobian minors, matching-polynomial identities, and cyclic block decomposition.   • The Wallace problem in ZFC — Establishes that every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum admits a Hausdorff countably compact group topology with no nontrivial convergent sequences, including the continuum-indexed rational direct sum and additive reals. It also constructs a commutative Tychonoff countably compact cancellative topological semigroup that is not a group. (Lean Pool PR #397)

  • Improved asymptotic bounds for binary and spherical codes — For 0 < δ < 1/2, proves binaryRate δ ≤ combinedVariationalRate δ < mrrwRate δ, giving a strict improvement over the MRRW rate in this range. Companion spherical-hierarchy results include an eventual kissing-number bound of 2^(0.39661 n). (Lean Pool PR #394)

  • Quantum parallel repetition — Proves a universal exponential decay bound for repeated entangled values of every finite game with nonempty answer alphabets and positive entangled-value gap, with exponent proportional to gap^13 / (gap + log(|A|·|B|)); it also proves the standard statement that every finite game with entangled value below one has exponential decay under parallel repetition. (Lean Pool PR #395)

  • Polynomial-factor hardness of the closest vector problem — Proves that Euclidean GapCVP with approximation factor n^(1/400) is NP-hard as a promise problem for positive-dimensional lattices with nonsingular integer bases, positive rational radii, and integer targets. The project also proves NP-hardness for binary nearest codeword, binary syndrome decoding, and finite rational p-norm GapCVP. (Lean Pool PR #396)

New projects

  • The optimal exponent relating sumsets and difference sets — For every finite set of integers A with at least two elements, the exponent log(|A+A|/|A|) / log(|A−A|/|A|) is strictly less than 2, while an explicit base-39 family of finite sets has exponents tending to 2; hence 2 is the supremum over all such A and is never attained, and one explicit set has exponent within 10^(−999) of 2. The import is the upstream row-and-column construction, not the paper's base-12 automaton construction or its quantitative cardinality estimates (Lin–Li, arXiv:2607.27199; Lean proofs AI-generated per the paper). (Lean Pool PR #445)

  • Chaos and the Julia set of the complex exponential — Proves Misiurewicz's theorem that the Julia set of z ↦ exp z is the whole plane, with the Fatou set defined by local normality of the Riemann-sphere-valued iterates, and that exp is chaotic in Devaney's sense (continuous, dense periodic points, topologically transitive). Escaping points and repelling periodic points are dense, uncountably many points have dense forward orbit, and for every nonempty open U and compact K omitting 0 all sufficiently large iterates of U cover K; the normal-sequence restriction and quantitative open-mapping lemmas are stated for arbitrary separated uniform codomains. Follows Shen–Rempe-Gillen (arXiv:1408.1129); Lean proofs AI-generated under Lasse Rempe's direction, with the initial six-lemma architecture adapted from Harrison's HOL Light development. (Lean Pool PR #438)

  • Chvátal's conjecture and sharp Boolean correlation — Proves Chvátal's conjecture as classically stated: for a hereditary (downward-closed) family D of subsets of a finite nonempty set, every intersecting subfamily of D has at most as many members as some star {S ∈ D : i ∈ S}, and one star is itself a largest intersecting subfamily. The route is Chang–Liu–Liu's sharp correlation inequality for increasing Boolean functions f, g on the cube (the Fourier energy of g weighted by the largest influence of f on each index set is at most the harmonic mean of Cov(f,g) and Cov(f,g*)), with equality for AND, the corollary Cov(f,g) ≥ (minimum influence of f)/4 for self-dual g, and a weighted star theorem for nonnegative decreasing weights (arXiv:2609.19123). Lean proofs generated by GPT-6 under Boon Suan Ho's direction; upstream claims no human expert review. (Lean Pool PR #443)

  • Asymptotically attaining the Moore bound — For each fixed k ≥ 1, the largest order n(k,d) of a finite simple graph with maximum degree at most d and extended diameter at most k satisfies n(k,d)/d^k → 1 as d → ∞, so the Moore bound is asymptotically attained; for ℓ ≥ 2 the edge analogue with line-graph diameter at most ℓ has liminf h(ℓ,d)/d^ℓ ≥ 1. The witnesses are regular halved-flag graphs over every finite field with exact order, degree cap, and diameter, and the passage through all d uses a prime in (x, (1+ε)x) proved from the vendored PrimeNumberTheoremAnd modules (Cames van Batenburg–Korsky, arXiv:2608.03965; mixed human/AI provenance). (Lean Pool PR #444)

  • Finite witnesses and the width hierarchy for language generation — For any family H of infinite languages over a countably infinite universe, H is generatable in the limit (one generator, fixed before the target, eventually outputs unseen elements of the target on every exact presentation) exactly when H admits a finite positive-witness assignment whose nonempty active subfamilies always have infinite common intersection. The separation-width invariant realizes every value 0, 1, 2, …, ω, ω+1, and generation is equivalent to width at most ω; the paper's density-one and Turing-computability results are not formalized (Li–Han–Jiang–Gao, arXiv:2609.10525, over a Core library by Shuangping Li and Peng Zhang; AI-assisted under human direction). (Lean Pool PR #437)

  • Serre's mass formula for totally ramified local-field extensions — For a nonarchimedean local field K (Mathlib's IsNonarchimedeanLocalField) with residue field of size q and every n ≥ 1, the sum of q^(−c(L)) over the totally ramified degree-n subextensions L of a separable closure equals n, where c(L) = d(L) − n + 1 and d(L) is the discriminant exponent; summing 1/(|Aut_K(L)| · q^(c(L))) over isomorphism-class representatives gives 1. Also proved: d(L) ≥ n − 1, c(L) = 0 exactly in the tame case, the set of such extensions is infinite exactly when K has equal characteristic p with p ∣ n, and each isomorphism class has n/|Aut_K(L)| members; supporting results include Eisenstein monogenicity, Newton–Hensel lifting over complete DVRs, and Haar volumes of lattices (Serre 1978; Lean proofs AI-generated under Hyeon Seung-Hyeon's direction). (Lean Pool PR #439)

  • Jordan–Schönflies theorem — In ℝ², every homeomorphism between two Jordan curves (images of continuous loops injective on [0,1), with no polygonal restriction) extends to a self-homeomorphism of the plane. The development includes the Jordan curve theorem in the form it uses: the complement of a Jordan curve has a connected bounded inside and a connected unbounded outside, each with the curve as its frontier (130 modules; Lean proofs AI-generated under Álvaro Begué's direction). (Lean Pool PR #435)

  • Craig interpolation and Beth definability for propositional dynamic logic — For full PDL with tests and Kleene star, if φ → ψ holds at every world of every Kripke model, there is a formula θ with φ → θ and θ → ψ valid whose atomic propositions and atomic programs all occur in both φ and ψ; local Beth definability follows: a formula that implicitly defines a propositional letter p yields an explicit definition of p in its vocabulary without p. The interpolant comes from uniform cyclic tableaux, with tableau soundness and completeness (consistent ↔ satisfiable for free sequents); the results are existence statements with no extraction algorithm or complexity bound (Borzechowski et al., arXiv:2503.13276; human contributors and Aristotle; reuses the finite game determinacy already pooled in Lean4GlCoalgebras). (Lean Pool PR #440)

  • Komlós and Beck–Fiala bounds with constant 36 — For any finite family of vectors in ℝᵈ, each of Euclidean norm at most 1, there are signs ±1 making every coordinate of their signed sum at most 36 in absolute value, independently of the dimension and family size; for a finite hypergraph with each vertex in at most t edges, this gives a vertex colouring with every edge sum bounded by 36√t. The development follows Karingula–Lovett (ECCC TR26-188), using discrete squared-tent weights, and includes a signed-sum/convex-hull theorem for finitely supported probability distributions on arbitrary real modules. Lean proofs produced by AI under Gabriel Dahia's direction. (Lean Pool PR #456)

  • Nivat's conjecture — For a configuration c : ℤ² → A over any finite alphabet, if some rectangle of positive integer dimensions m × n has at most mn distinct patterns across all lattice translations, then c(z+h) = c(z) for every z and some nonzero lattice vector h. This proves the full rectangular-complexity implication, with one global period; the argument descends in rectangle area through Laurent-polynomial annihilators and includes the two-factor periodicity theorem. The manuscript and Lean proofs were AI-generated under Boon Suan Ho's direction. (Lean Pool PR #451)

  • The Erdős–Sós tree-containment theorem — For every tree T on t ≥ 2 vertices, a finite simple graph on n ≥ 1 vertices containing no injective copy of T has 2|E| ≤ (t−2)n; thus more than (t−2)n/2 edges force a copy of every such tree, as a subgraph with no inducedness requirement. The import also proves the exact Erdős Problem 548 statement: for n ≥ k+1, at least (k−1)n/2 + 1 edges force every tree on k+1 vertices. The proof uses permutation-word double counting and rooted-tree induction; upstream attributes the Lean proof to GPT-6 Astra in the FrontierMath Erdős benchmark, in Tom Adamczewski's repository. (Lean Pool PR #452)

  • Finite max-flow/min-cut — Every finite network with nonnegative real capacities and distinct source and sink admits a feasible flow and a source–sink cut of equal value and capacity; weak duality makes them a maximum flow and a minimum cut. The reusable network, skew-flow, cut and residual-reachability interfaces support maximum-flow attainment by compactness and the augmenting-path proof, without an integrality assumption on capacities (Juan Pablo Traverso Gianini and Aristotle). (Lean Pool PR #432)

  • Even graphs decompose into edge-disjoint cycles — Every finite loopless edge set with even degree at each vertex is the union of edge-disjoint simple cycles of length at least three. The development also constructs simultaneous fixed-point-free involutions pairing the incident edges at each vertex, and exposes both conclusions through Mathlib's SimpleGraph degree and edge-set APIs (Juan Pablo Traverso Gianini and Aristotle). (Lean Pool PR #433)

Iterated lifts yield sizes 810ᵉ at degree bound 8e for e ≥ 1 and 27·810ᵉ at degree bound 8e+4 for e ≥ 0, and prove liminf log D(n)/(n log 3) ≥ 16/21 for the maximum possible cardinality D(n). Euler’s pentagonal theorem follows by specialization and is also proved through Franklin’s involution on distinct-part partitions; the project includes analytic Cauchy identities and convergence lemmas, alongside pentagonal results that overlap the existing pooled development.   • A complex-analytic atlas on the six-sphere — Proves that the unit sphere S⁶ ⊂ ℝ⁷, with its standard topology, admits a complex-analytic atlas of complex dimension three.   • Dilatations of categories and commutative rings — Constructs categories of permitted fractions and proves unique factorization of functors when localization at the image denominators is faithful and the image numerator sieves lie in the corresponding denominator-generated sieves.   • Kolokolnikov’s ACMAX conjecture — For every n ≥ 4, a simple graph with n vertices and exactly 2(n−2) edges has second-smallest combinatorial-Laplacian eigenvalue at most 2, and K₂,ₙ₋₂ attains 2. The proof covers all such orders and includes Rayleigh-quotient bounds and test-vector certificates for arbitrary finite nonempty vertex types. (Lean Pool PR #458)

  • Low-weight Pauli dynamics and truncation error — For an n-qubit operator O supported on Pauli weights at most kₒ, repeating a fixed block of Γ ≥ 1 layers, each containing Hermitian Pauli rotations with pairwise disjoint supports and weight at most kₕ ≥ 2, and truncating to weight kₒ + m(kₕ−1) after each of r blocks, gives normalized Pauli 2-norm error at most (2Γ(kₕ−1)αt)^(m+1) · (e(m+1))^(kₒ/(kₕ−1)) · ‖O‖, provided α > 0, t ≥ 0, every rotation angle satisfies |sin θ| ≤ a ≤ αt/r with a ≥ 0, and the integer parameters satisfy m ≥ 1, r ≥ max(5, m), rΓ ≥ 8(m+1)², and r ≥ 8e²(kₒ+kₕ−1)αt. Γ counts all layer occurrences, including repetitions; the result controls circuit truncation in this norm, while expectation-value accuracy and Hamiltonian approximation are outside its scope. The development also supplies a finite rectangular Schur test bounding the Euclidean operator norm by √(RC) from nonnegative absolute row- and column-sum bounds R and C. (Lean Pool PR #522)

  • Block sensitivity can exceed spectral sensitivity squared — Constructs a total Boolean function on 14,011 blocks of 144 bits with block sensitivity bs(f) ≥ 14,011 and squared spectral sensitivity λ(f)² ≤ U = 7149 + 2√150108, and proves the strict separation λ(f)^2.12 < bs(f). A single seed yields, for every natural m, an m-fold self-composition Fₘ satisfying bs(Fₘ) ≥ (14011/U)^m · λ(Fₘ)², with 14011/U > 1.768; the development also proves spectral-sensitivity multiplicativity under block composition for arbitrary finite Boolean coordinate types. (Lean Pool PR #527)
